items.Sentence: Preliminary Treatment at Headworks – Removes coarse solids (by bar screening), sand and silt (by grit removal system) from wastewater.
Preliminary Treatment at Headworks – Removes coarse solids (by bar screening), sand and silt (by grit removal system) from wastewater.
Primary Sedimentation – Removes solids from the wastewater by gravity. The heavier solids settle and are scraped out of the primary sedimentation basin.
Activated Sludge Biological Treatment – Activated sludge consists of microorganisms that consume non-settleable and dissolved organic contaminants which form a settleable floc.
Secondary Clarification – Removes biological floc from the wastewater which then mostly becomes part of the waste sludge.
Chemicals such as aluminum sulfate (alum) may be added as part of the treatment process to encourage floc formation and enhance solids removal.
Tertiary Treatment – The filtration process is used to remove or reduce suspended or colloidal matter from a liquid stream by passing the water through a bed of graded granular material.
Microfiltration Feedwater Wet Well – Tertiary treated wastewater is diverted to this wet well.
The effluent to the microfiltration station is pretreated with sodium hypochlorite and aqua ammonia to prevent biofouling and then fed into automatic self-cleaning 500-micron strainers.
The wastewater flow from the wet well is then split into two parallel trains, containing eighteen (18) parallel Memcor microfiltration units in total.

Prior to entering the RO process train, the pH of the treated water from the microfiltration units may need to be adjusted with sulfuric acid to protect the RO filters from calcium carbonate precipitation.

The AOP includes two (2) low-pressure ultraviolet (UV) irradiation trains and hypochlorous acid addition. The AOP is used to disinfect RO permeate and destroy some constituents of emerging concern (CECs) that pass through RO membranes...
The effluent to the microfiltration station is pretreated with sodium hypochlorite and aqua ammonia to prevent biofouling...

AWPF Pumping Station – The AOP effluent is stabilized and then distributed from the AWPF Pumping Station. Six product water pumps in the Product Water Tank transfer the finished product water into the distribution system.
Sodium hydroxide and calcium chloride are added in the Stabilization Tank to increase the pH of the AOP effluent to protect the LADPW’s distribution and injection system.

However, the land application option is currently unavailable.
